payload.statement:
# HOL Council — ch01b Opening Fiction ("The Last Ember")

Chapter under review: ch01b (quarto-book/chapters/01b-opening-fiction.qmd), "The Last Ember", 123 lines. The book's opening fiction: a short story in which the party (Kael the dwarf Blade, Lyra the halfling Odd, Roric the Protector, Zara the storm-speaker) breaks a warding glyph in a sealed temple and kills a many-legged guardian. It is the first fiction the reader meets after the front matter, and the canon reference for the party's identities and play styles (ch01's Example of Play points readers here: "You'll meet Kael and Lyra in the opening story").

Task: audit the chapter as a publishable unit and produce a disposition plan. Each member audits through their own lens (see role card) and files ONE finding:
  stance support = the chapter holds on this lens as written
  stance refute  = the chapter must change; name the fix and its scope
Findings cite [01b-opening-fiction.qmd:line]. Mechanics findings state the broken value and the expected value.

Cross-chapter canon anchors (use the AUTHORITATIVE chapters as reference, not this chapter):
- discipline taxonomy = ch08 (08-disciplines.qmd): 19 named Disciplines in 4 categories. Relevant names: Armor (one Discipline, Defense category, "heavy armor proficiency, damage soaking"), Wind (Nature category), Energy (Arcane category), Knowledge (Arcane category), Protection (Defense category). There is no "Armor Disciplines" plural taxonomy beyond the single Armor Discipline; ranks within one Discipline max at 3 (the Master ladder).
- class starting bundles = ch08 table (~lines 73-80): Protector = 1 any Weapon + 1 Armor; Arcanist = 1 Fire + 1 Energy; Shepherd = 1 Protection + 1 Animal; Leader = 1 Tactics + 1 Protection; Unbalanced = 1 Fire + 1 Water (or Earth/Wind); Blade = Blades (1) + Stealth (1).
- party canon = ch02 (templates/walkthroughs), ch13-combat.qmd (initiative example lines ~348-432: Kael (Blade) 13, Lyra (Odd) 16, Roric (Protector) 7, Knight of the Iron Circle Challenge 3; Kael's longsword + buckler, Roric's warhammer and Brawn +2), ch05-classes.qmd (class flavor and favored skills), ch01-introduction.qmd (Example of Play: Kael dwarf Blade with longsword, Brawn +1; Lyra halfling Odd, Agility +2, Stealth Adept +2; party stated as veteran adventurers several levels in).
- known open question (decisions-pending #73, for context only, do not re-litigate): the Blade class flavor (ch05: shadow-assassin, light blades) vs Kael's vanguard portrayal in this chapter and his longsword (a Heavy Weapon). That tension is already logged for Bruce; audit this chapter's text on its own merits.

Book conventions every lens applies: zero em-dashes in the book (restructure sentences instead of find-replace); no stale or retired vocabulary (the role label is DA, never GM); placeholder content (TBD, "final art TBD") is ACCEPTABLE in a draft build and is NOT a defect to fix now (flag only if a placeholder is wrong or inconsistent); the one-roll principle (the hit roll IS the damage roll; no separate damage dice); flat damage budgets (Novice 2/4/6, Adept 6/9/12, Master 9/15/21); success tiers Weak 1-8 / Standard 9-14 / Strong 15-18+; Adept gates at level 3, Master at level 7; card costs flat 2/4/8 DP.

Specific areas worth checking (findings are yours to file or dismiss):
- line 19: "Armor Disciplines, three of them" — Roric is described as having three Armor Disciplines. Check this phrasing against the ch08 taxonomy (Armor is one Discipline; three ranks in one Discipline is the Master shape, but the wording "three of them" reads like three separate Disciplines named Armor).
- line 21 and line 47: Zara "had three Wind Disciplines" / "Three Wind Disciplines didn't just summon a breeze" — check the same plural-discipline phrasing against the taxonomy (Wind is one Discipline).
- line 27: the inline roll narration "3d6: 5, 4, 6, 15 plus Brawn plus skill, Strong" — check the arithmetic (5+4+6 = 15; 15 + Brawn + skill is at least 15, so Strong is consistent with the tier table; the narration gives no explicit modifiers, so it is a summary, not a worked example — flag only if it misstates a tier or contradicts a canon number).
- lines 1-5: the heading "# The Last Ember {#sec-chapter-opening-fiction}" AND a typst block "#label(\"sec-chapter-opening-fiction\")" define the same anchor twice. Check whether the duplicate label definition is a defect (redundant, or a render warning).
- the anchor sec-chapter-opening-fiction: no other chapter cross-references it (grep the book). An orphaned forward-looking anchor is not itself a defect, but note if it is dead weight or if a chapter that should link here (e.g. ch01's "You'll meet Kael and Lyra in the opening story") does not.
- em-dashes: count and locate every em-dash in the chapter; the zero law applies to fiction prose as well as rules prose.
- Kael's longsword (lines 27, 45, 61, 87): a Heavy Weapon in the hands of the Blade; the ch01/ch05 tension is already logged (#73) — audit only what is broken in THIS chapter's own text.
- Zara's class: the fiction shows her as the party's storm-speaker (Wind + Energy) but never names her class; check whether any authoritative chapter (ch02, ch13) names her, and whether the fiction's portrayal contradicts it (Unbalanced's starting bundle includes Wind as an option).

Disposition tiers (the librarian synthesizes these in the recommendation):
  TIER 1 mechanical — chapter-local, zero mechanics change, no content judgment (heading/label, wording, em-dashes, table rows, stale refs, page flow).
  TIER 2 substantive — rewrites or multi-sentence fixes that change content but not rules (a line rephrased to match canon, a paragraph restructured).
  TIER 3 design decisions — anything that touches rules, canon identities, or book-wide convention; route to decisions-pending for Bruce, with a recommended default.

It defines one cross-reference target, sec-chapter-opening-fiction, and that target is currently unreferenced by any other chapter, so the entry is inert dead weight rather than a live link. The convention that pairs a heading anchor with a typst label block is applied uniformly across the book, so it is not a local defect here. None of these is a chapter-local mechanical break, so the unit holds on the documentation lens and is logged as a disposition note for the record, not a required change to this file.

payload.argument: Tested the plural-discipline phrasing, the inline 3d6 roll, and Zara's unnamed class as the three load-bearing fiction-as-rules risks. The plural phrasing holds: the book's own ch08 example uses the identical 'N X Disciplines' wording for rank-count inside a single Discipline, so 'three Armor' (01b-opening-fiction.qmd:19) and 'three Wind' (01b-opening-fiction.qmd:21, :47) read as Master-rank depth, not three separate Disciplines. The 3d6 line holds: 5+4+6 is 15, plus Brawn and skill lands Strong, matching the tier table, and it is a summary with no misstated canon number. But Zara's class breaks. This chapter is routed as the party identity reference (ch01 points readers to the opening story to meet the party), and it depicts Zara as a Wind+Energy storm-speaker who summons hurricanes. The one other chapter that names her, ch03-attributes.qmd:158, calls her a Shepherd of the wild gods, and a Shepherd is a divine guide with Protection and Animal (ch05, ch08), not an elemental caster. A player or DA reading this fiction as rules would build Zara as an elemental storm caster, an identity the book contradicts elsewhere, and no in-fiction line disambiguates. Fix and scope: TIER 3 canon identity, chapter-local to 01b-opening-fiction.qmd. Either reconcile Zara's depiction with the Shepherd identity (ch03-attributes.qmd:158, ch05:30, ch08:76) or, as the recommended default, name her class in-fiction at the point she first acts (around lines 21 and 47) so the fiction and the ch03 example cannot diverge. Route to decisions-pending for Bruce if a new class anchor is preferred over editing the fiction.

payload.argument: Every contested anchor in the opening fiction checks out against the authoritative chapters, so the chapter holds on the research lens as written. The inline roll at [01b-opening-fiction.qmd:27] narrates a 5-4-6 roll totalling 15 plus Brawn plus skill and calls the outcome Strong, which matches the ch06 success-tier table (Strong is 15-18+); it is a summary line, not a worked example, and misstates no tier and contradicts no canon number. The plural-discipline phrasing at [01b-opening-fiction.qmd:19] ('Armor Disciplines, three of them') and at [01b-opening-fiction.qmd:21] and [01b-opening-fiction.qmd:47] ('three Wind Disciplines') is not an invented taxonomy: ch08's own worked idiom counts ranks inside a single Discipline using the same plural form (a hero with '3 Blade Disciplines', '3 Fire Disciplines'), ch07 repeats it for the longsword gate, and ch08 states the cap as three ranks in any one Discipline. Since Armor and Wind are each a single Discipline, 'three X Disciplines' reads as three ranks in that one Discipline, the Master shape, and is canon-consistent rather than a three-separate-Disciplines claim. The double anchor at [01b-opening-fiction.qmd:1-5] (a heading anchor plus a matching typst label block) is the universal book pattern, present identically across all anchored chapters including ch08, so it is a shared convention, not a chapter-local defect. The chapter also contains zero em-dashes, satisfying the zero-em-dash law, and neither ch02 nor ch13 names Zara's class, so the fiction's classless storm-speaker portrayal contradicts no authoritative text. No change is required from the research lens; the only residual note is that the anchor sec-chapter-opening-fiction currently has no inbound cross-reference (ch01 points to the story in prose only), which the run brief itself classifies as not a defect.

payload.argument: I hold and sharpen my round-1 Zara refute, and I test the two supports that contest it. Neither actually engages the ch03 anchor. The research support surveyed only ch02 and ch13, found no class name there, and concluded the storm-speaker portrayal contradicts no authoritative text; that conclusion is incomplete, because ch03-attributes.qmd:158 explicitly labels her a Shepherd of the wild gods, backed by a divine Reason and Religion roll. The mechanics support dodges the identity question by arguing Unbalanced's starting bundle lawfully covers her Wind ranks; but Disciplines being purchasable by some class does not answer which class she is, and her shown Disciplines (Wind plus Energy) sit outside the Shepherd's Protection-and-Animal bundle, so the Disciplines point away from Shepherd, not toward it. The conflict is therefore hard, not a soft tension: one chapter casts her as an elemental storm-caster, the other as a divine guide with no elemental start. Scope and fix stay TIER 3 and chapter-local to 01b-opening-fiction.qmd: reconcile her depiction with the Shepherd identity, or, recommended default, name her class at her first action (around lines 21 and 47) so the fiction and the ch03 example cannot diverge; route to Bruce only if a new class anchor is preferred. I also stress-test the two colleague refutes as devil's advocate. On f-005 (terminology), the supports' strongest counter is real: ch08:23 uses the identical 'N X Disciplines' idiom to count ranks inside one Discipline, so a first-pass reader does not break and the defect is real only at the ch08 reveal; what breaks if it is left unfixed is a first-time player who builds the party from this fiction before reading ch08, reading 'three Wind' and 'three Armor' as three separate Disciplines, and the author's own fix is entangled with f-002, because rewording Zara's Wind lines to 'ranks within one Discipline' preserves an elemental identity she should not have if ch03 holds, so the fix is safe on Roric's Armor line (19) but wrong on Zara's lines (21, 47) until the identity is settled. On f-006 (dead anchor), nothing breaks in the printed artifact, the layout lens verified clean pages 28-32 and print placement holds, so the cost is confined to linked or HTML output where a reader cannot jump to the story the onboarding prose promises; that break is real but ch01-local, and the contrarian trap is the build's duplicate-label warning, which is a book-wide pattern every chapter emits, so filing the dead anchor as a chapter defect mis-scopes a shared convention.

payload.argument: Round 1 supported this chapter on the research lens, but that verdict rested on an incomplete cross-chapter audit: I checked only ch02 and ch13 for Zara's class, found no naming, and treated that as proof the fiction's classless storm-speaker portrayal contradicted no canon. Re-checking the full book against the authoritative chapters in round 2 shows ch03 names her directly as a divine class and the fiction's elemental profile conflicts with it, so the chapter does not hold on the research lens as written.
